keyChanges.title: Model S/X Production Line Decommissioned in 46 Days at Fremont
keyChanges.description: Tesla completed teardown of original Model S and Model X assembly line at Fremont Factory in just 46 days, involving removal of robotic arms, conveyors, and concrete pits. The space will be repurposed for Optimus humanoid robot production targeting 1M units/year capacity. Final S/X vehicles rolled off the line in early May 2026, with Optimus production on the converted line expected to begin in late July or August 2026. This represents Tesla's strategic pivot away from low-volume luxury sedans (<3% of 2025 deliveries) toward high-volume robotics manufacturing.

positive_signals: Rapid 46-day factory conversion demonstrates operational efficiency
Strategic reallocation of factory space to higher-volume Optimus production (1M target vs <20K S/X annual)
Fremont Optimus production starting late July/August 2026
negative_signals: Elimination of flagship Model S/X vehicles after 14+ years of production
Loss of premium vehicle segment revenue (though <3% of total deliveries)
Temporary production capacity reduction during transition period

keyChanges.title: Modest Full-Year 2026 Growth Despite Strong Q2 Performance
keyChanges.description: While Tesla crushed Q2 2026 delivery expectations with 480,126 vehicles delivered (+25% YoY, beating consensus of 406K by 18%), full-year 2026 guidance remains concerning at only 1.69M units (~3-5% growth vs 1.64M in 2025). This represents a significant moderation from historical Tesla growth rates and analyst expectations have been downgraded by 35K vehicles since March 2026. The modest guidance persists despite Q2's strong performance and successful inventory drawdown of 28,368 units.

positive_signals: Q2 2026: 480,126 deliveries beat consensus by 18% (vs 406K expected)
Successfully cleared Q1 inventory backlog of 50K+ units
Strong 25% YoY growth in Q2 vs 2025
Energy storage deployment at 13.5 GWh (2nd best quarter ever, +40% YoY)
negative_signals: Full-year 2026 forecast downgraded from 1.69M to 1.65M (35K reduction since March)
Only 3-5% annual growth projected vs historical 50%+ CAGR target
Capital expenditure increased to $25B+ with negative free cash flow projected for Q2-Q4
Production (451,758) significantly trails delivery capacity, indicating conservative manufacturing outlook

keyChanges.title: Giga Berlin 20% Production Increase to 73K Units/Quarter
keyChanges.description: Tesla announced a 20% production boost at Gigafactory Berlin starting July 2026, targeting 73,000 Model Y units per quarter (up from record 61,000 in Q1 2026). The facility will hire 1,000 new employees (onboarding began in May) and convert 500 temporary workers to permanent positions. This expansion follows strong European demand recovery with Germany registrations quadrupling to 9,252 units in March 2026 and overall March registrations up 117% YoY. However, Berlin still operates below theoretical capacity despite this increase.

positive_signals: 20% production increase to 73K Model Y/quarter starting July 2026
European demand recovery: Germany registrations up 4x in March 2026
Q1 2026 record 61,000 vehicles produced at Berlin
Management confidence in sustained European demand
negative_signals: Still operating below factory's theoretical maximum capacity
Expansion only returns Berlin to mid-2023 production rates
Requires significant hiring/training period (May-July) before full ramp
